overview.headline: Hash tables map keys to array positions with collision handling

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a hash table maps keys to array positions using hash functions.
keyPoints.quote: A dictionary in which keys are mapped to array positions by hash functions.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a collision occurs when keys of different items map to the same position.
keyPoints.quote: Having the keys of more than one item map to the same position is called a collision.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that collision resolution schemes include open addressing, chaining, and a special overflow area.
keyPoints.quote: There are many collision resolution schemes, but they may be divided into open addressing, chaining, and keeping one special overflow area.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that perfect hashing avoids collisions but can be time-consuming to create.
keyPoints.quote: Perfect hashing avoids collisions, but may be time-consuming to create.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that hash table operations may be constant time if the table is big enough or grows.
keyPoints.quote: Complexity depends on the hash function and collision resolution scheme, but may be constant (Θ(1)) if the table is big enough or grows.
